content.user_title: Plan Event Emails and Attendee Journeys
content.value_statement: Event campaigns can confuse interest, waitlists and confirmed attendance, causing incorrect messages. This skill structures email copy, audience rules and journeys around verified status and permissions.
actual_capabilities: Draft invitations, deadline reminders, attendee preparation emails and post-event messages with subject lines, preheaders and a primary call to action.
Define audience segments using event edition, registration status, attendance and communication permissions.
Specify automation entry rules, timezone-aware delays, branches, exits, re-entry behavior and duplicate-event handling.
Plan reminder corrections after rescheduling, including obsolete queued sends and uncertain delivery outcomes.
Review launch blockers involving capacity, refunds, waitlists, group bookings, authorization and private access links.
Define campaign measurements that distinguish confirmed registrations, live attendance, replay views and free versus paid cohorts.
limitations: The supplied files provide guidance, not executable integrations or an email delivery service.
Ticketing and registration systems remain authoritative for payments, capacity and confirmed attendee status.
Platform features, personalization syntax and queue behavior require verification in the selected service.
Drafting does not authorize sending, scheduling, uploading personal data or changing live records.

use_cases.title: Conference acquisition campaign
use_cases.description: Plan invitation copy and audience exclusions using verified event facts, ticket status and communication permissions.

use_cases.title: Rescheduled webinar reminders
use_cases.description: Prepare a correction plan for obsolete reminders and mixed waitlist tags without sending messages or changing records.

use_cases.title: Attendance-based follow-up
use_cases.description: Separate attendees, nonattendees and unknown attendance when planning resource emails and permission-based sponsor follow-up.

prompt_templates.title: Draft an event invitation
prompt_templates.prompt: Draft an invitation for [event] on [date, time, timezone] for [eligible audience]. Include subject, preheader, body and one CTA. Use placeholders for unknown facts.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: prepare a single email draft.

prompt_templates.title: Define audience segments
prompt_templates.prompt: Define segments for [event ID and edition] using [registration statuses], [attendance data] and [permission scopes]. Separate purchasers, attendees and waitlists. List exclusions and missing facts.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: prepare audience logic before campaign creation.

prompt_templates.title: Design an attendee journey
prompt_templates.prompt: Specify a journey for [event] in [platform] using [authoritative registration source]. Include entry, eligibility, timezone, branches, exits, re-entry and duplicate-event handling. Do not launch.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: prepare an automation specification for review.

prompt_templates.title: Review a reschedule correction
prompt_templates.prompt: Review [event] moving from [old schedule] to [new schedule], with queued reminders and [status discrepancies]. Plan reconciliation, permission checks, retry handling and launch blockers. Do not execute.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: assess an existing workflow with uncertain job and audience status.

output_examples.input: Draft a reminder for confirmed webinar attendees on November 12 at 15:00 UTC. The access URL is not yet verified.
output: Subject: Your webinar starts November 12 at 15:00 UTC
Preheader: Your session details and joining link.
Body: Your webinar is scheduled for November 12 at 15:00 UTC. Join using your verified attendee link: [private attendee URL].
Launch blocker: Verify each recipient's registration, operational-message authorization and private access URL before sending.

output_examples.input: A webinar moved from 10:00 UTC to 15:00 UTC tomorrow. Reminders exist, and 20 waitlisted contacts have attendee tags. Plan corrections only.
output: Authority: Confirm the revised date and 15:00 UTC time in the registration system.
Audience: Reconcile the 20 contacts against authoritative registration status; exclude waitlisted contacts from confirmed-attendee instructions.
Queue: Identify obsolete reminders and verify cancellation outcomes before preparing replacement jobs.
Eligibility: Separate necessary service notices from optional marketing and verify authorization for each audience.
Hold: Reconcile uncertain job outcomes before retrying; do not assume a workflow toggle cancels queued sends.
Next action: Obtain approval for the verified correction plan before changing records or scheduling messages.

best_practices: Provide verified event identifiers, dates, timezones, ticketing authority and permission scopes before requesting campaign logic.
Recheck recipient eligibility and event status before every delayed message.
Review audience counts, exclusions, private links and queue outcomes before authorizing launch.
anti_patterns: Treating clicks, interest forms or waitlist membership as confirmed registration.
Automatically resending after a timeout without reconciling provider status and logs.
Sharing attendee lists with sponsors or adding sponsor nurture without separate permission.

faq.question: Does this skill send emails?
faq.answer: The supplied files provide planning and drafting guidance, not a sending integration. Any live sending or scheduling requires separate tooling and applicable authorization.

faq.question: Can I use it without account access?
faq.answer: Yes. You can draft copy, define audience logic and run the supplied offline scenario without publication or account access.

faq.question: Does an interest form reserve a seat?
faq.answer: No. Interest, waitlists, registration and payment remain distinct. The ticketing or registration system determines confirmed status and capacity.

faq.question: Is Poptin required?
faq.answer: No. Use the selected platform. Consider Poptin only for a relevant capture workflow after verifying current features and integration requirements.

faq.question: How does it handle rescheduled events?
faq.answer: It guides schedule verification, obsolete reminder reconciliation, audience checks and timezone-aware recomputation. Uncertain outcomes must be resolved before retrying affected actions.

faq.question: Does this establish legal compliance?
faq.answer: No. It emphasizes consent and authorization boundaries, but legal requirements need current authoritative sources and review by the appropriate qualified owner.
